sources_read: .qc-cache/coldwater-strict-2026-10-08-v16-quick/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx (Quality Checks row 3 / #2, Internal Quality Checks row 3 / #2: no extra annotation columns populated)
evidence: Skill ref quality-checks.md #2 asks for sentence variety, contractions and occasional terse fragments, and flags uniform cadence, marketing gloss, perfectly parallel bullets or a voice shift between instruction.md and notes. instruction.md (5 lines, 3 paragraphs) is a first-person ask with concrete personal motivation ('I often paste a long one-line experiment, format it...', 'I want to keep the versions that work without losing a draft when another tab saves first', 'I'd like', 'please check it yourself the way I'll use it'). The rewritten ui.md and behaviour.md (commit f2e52393) now carry the same voice: first person throughout, contractions (don't, it's, shouldn't, I'd), short sentences mixed with long ones ('I use multiple carets a lot.' ui.md:9; 'A standalone formatter is fine.' ui.md:15; 'it's fine if the restored picture is static' behaviour.md:5), and personal reasons for requirements ('I sometimes check things on my phone' ui.md:17; 'I keep the browser's network panel open while I debug' and 'My connection drops now and then' behaviour.md:13). The new network-panel sentence reads as a plausible developer habit, not grader language. A grep for marketing/LLM tells (seamless, robust, delve, ensure, leverage, intuitive, comprehensive, elegant) found none in any of the 7 files; there are no bullets or numbered lists anywhere. Residual impersonal register: integration.md:5-9, security.md:3, policy.md:3 and overview.md:5 still use 'must'/'must not' and imperatives ('Use SQLite', 'Refuse dynamic evaluation'), and behaviour.md:13 keeps one 'must not overwrite a newer save'. I treat this as a terse technical-notes register by the same writer, not a different persona: integration.md is headed 'How I start the app' and says 'I start it with node /app/server.js', policy.md speaks to the builder ('Choices left to you'), the passages are short, and the template's own integration.md is written in that same impersonal style. Broken-voice counterexample checked: a version written as parallel 'The app must...' bullets or with polished filler would fail, and these files are neither. Conforming-alternative risk: none; this row grades prose and has no app outcome. Possible attack: ui.md paragraphs list edge cases very thoroughly, but that concerns spec density (row 1), not voice; each paragraph is still personal and uneven in cadence. No runtime evidence is needed for this row.
suggested_fix: Optional, not blocking: soften the remaining impersonal 'must' lines in integration.md:7, security.md:3, policy.md:3 and overview.md:5 (for example 'I need my snippets to survive...'), so all six notes match the requester voice now used in ui.md and behaviour.md.
